Removes one or more players from the custom game. This action doesn't work on dummy bots.

The player or players to respawn.
Respawns one or more players at an appropriate spawn location with full health, even if they were already alive.

Instantly resurrects one or more players at the location they died with no transition.

The player or players whose ability charge count will be modified.

The player or players whose hero list is being set.

The player or players whose ammo will be set.
The index of the clip whose ammo will be set. 0 is the first clip, and 1 is the second (only used for Bastion's Sentry gun and Baptiste's Heal Grenades).
The ammo that will be set.
Sets the ammo of one or more players.
The player or players whose access to crouch is affected.

Enables or disables crouch for one or more players.
The player or players whose damage dealt will be set.

Sets the damage dealt of one or more players to a percentage of their raw damage dealt.
The player or players whose damage received will be set.

Sets the damage received of one or more players to a percentage of their raw damage received.

The player or players whose facing will be set.
The unit direction in which the player or players will face. This value is normalized internally.

Sets the facing of one or more players to the specified direction.
The player or players whose movement gravity will be set.
The percentage of regular movement gravity to which the player or players will set their personal movement gravity.
Sets the movement gravity for one or more players to a percentage of regular movement gravity.
The player or players whose healing dealt will be set.
Sets the healing dealt of one or more players to a percentage of their raw healing dealt.
The player or players whose healing received will be set.
The percentage of raw healing received to which the player or players will set their healing received.
Sets the healing received of one or more players to a percentage of their raw healing received.
The player or players whose health will be set.
How much health the player or players will have.

Sets the health of a player or players without affecting stats or granting damage/healing credit. This action only has an effect on living players. (For dead players, use the Resurrect Player action instead.)
The player or players who will become invisible.
Specifies for whom the player or players will be invisible.
Causes one or more players to become invisible to either all other players or just enemies.
The player or players whose access to jump is affected.
Specifies whether the player or players are able to use jump. Expects a boolean value such as true, false, or compare.
Enables or disables jump for one or more players.
The player or players whose jump vertical speed will be set.
The percentage of raw jump vertical speed to which the player or players will set their jump vertical speed.
Sets the jump vertical speed of one or more players to a percentage of their raw jump vertical speed.
The player or players whose knockback dealt will be set.
The percentage of raw knockback dealt to which the player or players will set their knockback dealt.
Sets the knockback dealt of one or more players to a percentage of their raw knockback dealt.
The player or players whose knockback received will be set.
The percentage of raw knockback received to which the player or players will set their knockback received.
Sets the knockback received of one or more players to a percentage of their raw knockback received.
The player or players whose max ammo will be set.
The index of the clip whose max ammo will be set. 0 is the first clip, and 1 is the second (only used for Bastion's Sentry gun and Baptiste's Heal Grenades).
The max ammo that will be set.
Sets the max ammo of one or more players.
The player or players whose max health will be set.
The percentage of raw max health to which the player or players will set their max health.
Sets the max health of one or more players as a percentage of their max health. This action will ensure that a player's current health will not exceed the new max health.
The player or players whose access to melee is affected.
Specifies whether the player or players are able to use melee. Expects a boolean value such as true, false, or compare.
Enables or disables melee for one or more players.
The player or players whose move speed will be set.
The percentage of raw move speed to which the player or players will set their move speed.
Sets the move speed of one or more players to a percentage of their raw move speed.
The player or players whose access to primary fire is affected.
Specifies whether the player or players are able to use primary fire. Expects a boolean value such as true, false, or compare.
Enables or disables primary fire for one or more players.
The player or players whose projectile gravity will be set.
The percentage of regular projectile gravity to which the player or players will set their personal projectile gravity.
Sets the projectile gravity for one or more players to a percentage of regular projectile gravity.
The player or players whose projectile speed will be set.
The percentage of regular projectile speed to which the player or players will set their personal projectile speed.
Sets the projectile speed for one or more players to a percentage of projectile speed.
The player or players whose access to reload is affected.
Specifies whether the player or players are able to use reload. Expects a boolean value such as True, False, or Compare.
Enables or disables Reload for one or more players.
The player or players whose respawn max time is being defined.
The duration between death and respawn in seconds.
Sets the duration between death and respawn for one or more players. For players that are already dead when this action is executed, the change takes effect on their next death.
The player or players whose score will be set.
The score that will be set.
Sets the score (kill count) of one or more players. This action only has an effect in free-for-all modes.
The player or players whose access to secondary fire is affected.

Specifies a player to be awarded assist credit should the affected player or players be killed while the status is in effect. An assister of null indicates no player will receive credit.
The status to be applied to the player or players. These behave similarly to statuses applied from hero abilities.
The duration of the status in seconds. To have a status that lasts until a clear status action is executed, provide an arbitrarily long duration such as 99999.
Applies a status to one or more players. This status will remain in effect for the specified duration or until it is cleared by the clear status action.
The player or players whose ultimate charge will be set.
The percentage of maximum charge.
Sets the ultimate charge for one or more players as a percentage of maximum charge.
The player or players whose access to their ultimate ability is affected.
Specifies whether the player or players are able to use their ultimate ability. Expects a boolean value such as true, false, or compare.
Enables or disables the ultimate ability of one or more players.
The player or players whose weapon will be set.
The number of the weapon to be equipped. 1 is the first weapon, and 2 is the second. If the specified weapon does not exist, players will use the default weapon.
Sets the weapon of one or more players.
The player or players that will begin accelerating.
The unit direction in which the acceleration will be applied. This value is normalized internally.
The rate of acceleration in meters per second squared. This value may need to be quite high in order to overcome gravity and/or surface friction.
The speed at which acceleration will stop for the player or players. It may not be possible to reach this speed due to gravity and/or surface friction.
Specifies whether direction is relative to world coordinates or the local coordinates of the player or players.
Specifies which of this action's inputs will be continuously reevaluated. This action will keep asking for and using new values from reevaluated inputs.
Starts accelerating one or more players in a specified direction.
The player or players whose cameras will be placed at the location.
The position of the camera. Reevaluates continuously.
Where the camera looks at. Reevaluates continuously.
How fast to blend the camera movement as positions change. 0 means do not blend at all, and just change positions instantly.
Places your camera at a location, facing a direction.
One or more players who will receive the damage over time.
The player who will receive credit for the damage. A damager of null indicates no player will receive credit.
The duration of the damage over time in seconds. To have a dot that lasts until stopped by script, provide an arbitrarily long duration such as 99999.
The damage per second for the damage over time.
Starts an instance of damage over time. This dot will persist for the specified duration or until stopped by script. To obtain a reference to this dot, use the last damage over time id value.
The player or players who will start turning.
The unit direction in which the player or players will eventually face. This value is normalized internally.
The turn rate in degrees per second.
Specifies whether direction is relative to world coordinates or the local coordinates of the player or players.
Specifies which of this action's inputs will be continuously reevaluated. This action will keep asking for and using new values from reevaluated inputs.
Starts turning one or more players to face the specified direction.
The player or players who are holding a button virtually.
The logical button that is being held virtually.
Forces one or more players to hold a button virtually until stopped by the stop holding button action.
The player or players who will be forced to be a specific hero.
The hero that the player or players will be forced to be.

Starts forcing one or more players to be a specific hero and, if necessary, respawns them immediately in their current location. This will be the only hero available to the player or players until the stop forcing player to be hero action is executed.

The name to be forced.
Starts forcing the name for the specified player or players (only works with AI and dummy bots).
The player or players who will have their outlines modified.
The viewing player or players for whom the viewed player's outlines will be modified.
Whether or not the specified player outlines should be visible.
The color of the specified player outlines, if they are visible.
The visibility type of the specified player outlines, if they are visible.
Starts forcing the visibility and color of the outlines of the specified viewed player or players from the perspective of one or more viewing players.
The player whose position will be forced. (The reevaluation option does not apply to this value.)
The position the player will occupy. If reevaluation is enabled, this value can be used to move the player around over time.
If this value is true, then the position will be reevaluated and applied to the player every frame. If this value is false, then the position is only evaluated once when the action begins.
Starts forcing a player to be in a given position. If reevaluation is enabled, then the position is evaluated every frame, allowing the player to be moved around over time.
The player or players whose movement will be forced or limited.
Sets the minimum run forward amount. 0 allows the player or players to stop while 1 forces full forward movement.
Sets the maximum run forward amount. 0 prevents the player or players from moving forward while 1 allows full forward movement.
Sets the minimum run backward amount. 0 allows the player or players to stop while 1 forces full backward movement.
Sets the maximum run backward amount. 0 prevents the player or players from moving backward while 1 allows full backward movement.
Sets the minimum run sideways amount. 0 allows the player or players to stop while 1 forces full sideways movement.
Sets the maximum run sideways amount. 0 prevents the player or players from moving SIDEWAYS while 1 allows full sideways movement.
Defines minimum and maximum movement input values for one or more players, possibly forcing or preventing movement.
The target Player or Players who will receive assist credit.

The Player or Players whose eliminations will grant assist credit to the Assisters. If the Target or Targets are allied to the Assister, this will be a defensive assist. Otherwise, this will be an offensive assist.
Specifies which of this Action's Inputs will be continuously reevaluated. This Action will keep asking for and using new Values from reevaluated Inputs.

Starts granting assist credit toward to one or more assisters when one or more targets are eliminated. A reference to this assist modification can be obtained from the getLastAssistId() value. This action will fail if too many assists have been started.
One or more players who will receive the heal over time.
The player who will receive credit for the healing. A healer of null indicates no player will receive credit.
The duration of the heal over time in seconds. To have a healing that lasts until stopped by script, provide an arbitrarily long duration such as 99999.
The healing per second for the heal over time.
Starts an instance of heal over time. This healing will persist for the specified duration or until stopped by script. To obtain a reference to this healing, use the last heal over time id value.
The player or players whose voice line sound will be modified.
The amount that the pitch of the voice will be raised (up to 1.5) or lowered (down to 0.5).
If true, Pitch Scalar is evaluated and updated every frame. If false, Pitch Scalar is evaluated once when the action executes.
Modifies the way hero voice lines sound for a player or players.
The player or players whose barriers will have their size modified.
The multiplier applied to the size of the barriers (0.5 halves the size, 2.0 doubles the size, etc.).
If this value is true, then scale will be reevaluated and applied to the player or players every frame. If this value is false, then the scale is only evaluated once when the action begins.
Starts modifying the size of barriers for a player or players.
The player or players whose size will be modified.
The multiplier applied to the size of the player or players (0.5 halves the size, 2.0 doubles the size, etc.).
If this value is true, then scale will be reevaluated and applied to the player or players every frame. If this value is false, then the scale is only evaluated once when the action begins.

Starts modifying the size of a player or players (including model, movement collision, hit detection, and certain abilities). Note that large players placed into complex environments will severely impact server load, so consider also applying the Disable Movement Collision With Environment action.
The player or players whose throttle will be set or added to.
The unit direction in which the throttle will be set or added to. This value is normalized internally.
The amount of throttle (or change to throttle). A value of 1 denotes full throttle.
Specifies whether direction is relative to world coordinates or the local coordinates of the player or players.
Specifies whether preexisting throttle is replaced or added to.
Specifies which of this action's inputs will be continuously reevaluated. This action will keep asking for and using new values from reevaluated inputs.
Sets or adds to the throttle (directional input control) of a player or players such that they begin moving in a particular direction. Any previous throttle in direction is cancelled.
The player or players whose throttle will be transformed.

The player or players will have their throttle X axis (left to right) multiplied by this value before the throttle is rotated to its new relative direction. This value is evaluated continuously (meaning it updates every frame).

The player or players will have their throttle Y axis (front to back) multiplied by this value before the throttle is rotated to its new relative direction. This value is evaluated continuously (meaning it updates every frame).

After the axis scalars are applied, the player or players will have their throttle transformed so that it is relative to this unit direction vector. For example, to make the throttle camera relative, provide the direction that the camera is facing. This value is evaluated continuously (meaning it updates every frame) and normalized internally.
Starts transforming (scaling and rotating) the throttle (directional input control) of a player or players. Cancels any existing start transforming throttle behavior.
The player or players who will stop accelerating.
Stops the acceleration started by the start accelerating action for one or more players.
The player or players whose scripted damage over time will stop.
Stops all damage over time started by start damage over time for one or more players.
The player or players whose scripted heal over time will stop.
Stops all heal over time started by start heal over time for one or more players.
The player or players whose cameras will be put back to the default view.
Restores the camera to the default view.
The player or players who will stop turning.
Stops the turning started by the start facing action for one or more players.
The player or players who are no longer holding a button virtually.
The logical button that is no longer being held virtually.
Undoes the effect of the start holding button action for one or more players.
The player or players who will no longer be forced to be a specific hero.
Stops forcing one or more players to be a specific hero. This will not respawn the player or players, but it will restore their hero availability the next time they go to select a hero.

The template is an OverPy expression with the following variables:

- `$rule`: the current rule name
- `$isDelimiter`: true if the rule is @Delimiter
- `$prefix`: the current prefix (set via `#!rulePrefix`)
- `$file`: the file name without extension
- `$path`: the relative path to the main file (backslashes replaced by slashes)
- Titlecase/lower/upper variations: `$prefixTitle`, `$prefixUpper`, `$prefixLower`, `$fileTitle`, `$fileUpper`, `$fileLower`, `$pathTitle`, `$pathUpper`, `$pathLower`

Examples :

- `#!rulePrefixTemplate f"[{$prefix}] {$rule}" if $prefix and $rule else $rule` (default): adds the prefix in square brackets before the rule name, if the prefix and rule name are not empty. This is the default if this directive is unspecified.
- `#!rulePrefixTemplate f"[{$pathTitle.replace('_', ' ')}] {$rule}" if $rule and not $isDelimiter else $rule`": if you have an `heroes/junker_queen.opy` file, will yield rule names like "[Heroes/Junker Queen] Spawn particles". This is the default if the directive is specified without an expression (just `#!rulePrefixTemplate`).

The expression has to evaluate to a string without arguments.

Add a rule to obtain an unsanitized '<' character which can be used to create <tx> and <fg> tags.

**WARNING**: The inserted rule creates a dummy bot then immediately destroys it. This has the side effect of triggering each-player rules and may break your gamemode (though if properly coded, it shouldn't).

The `__holygrail__` variable can be used to obtain the raw '<' character, although it is not necessary as OverPy will automatically take care of the conversion, meaning you can put raw texture tags in strings.

For color, use the <fgRRGGBBAA> tag, where RR/GG/BB are the hex color value, and AA is the hex transparency value (00 = transparent, FF = opaque).
Example: `print('<fgFF0000FF>Red text</fg>')`.

For textures, use the <TX> standalone tag, with the texture id as seen in https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/tx-reference-sheet.
Example: `print('<TXC0000000002DD21>')` will display the mouse cursor texture.

Additionally, you can use the `Texture` enum (such as `Texture.MOUSE_CURSOR`), and OverPy will automatically optimize it.

OverPy will also replace `'<tx1234>'` to the correct full texture id, but only if the entire tag is inside a string (`'<tx{}>'.format(id)` will not work, but `'<tx{}>'.format(1234)` will).
Suppresses the specified warnings globally across the program. Warnings must be separated by a space.

Stores the player's language in a variable using a rule which uses the `.startFacing()` function when the player spawns (the language is determined based on the player's facing direction).

If using translations, this can save a lot of elements. However, it will make translated strings not display correctly for spectators; you will have to wrap them with the `__` function (which behaves the same as the `_` function, except it will not use the `__languageIndex__` player variable).

If your gamemode changes the facing direction on spawn, you must modify it so that it changes it once `eventPlayer.__languageIndex__ != 1.1`.

You can specify `noDetectionRule` to not create the rule which sets the variable to the player's language, in which case you'll have to define the rule yourself; the variable must be set to the language as defined in the order specified in the `#!translations` directive, where the first language is index 1, and must be set to 1 by default if no language could be determined.

You can also specify `noTlErr` to have spectators view the default language when viewing a translated string (the `__languageIndex__` variable is now 0-indexed instead of 1-indexed). Keep in mind that, if translations aren't used properly, you may not see it if you playtest with the default language.

Setups the translation system. Arguments are the language codes separated by spaces.

For example:

`#!translations en fr es zh_cn`

Only the es_mx, es_es, zh_cn and zh_tw languages can be specified fully. For the rest, you can only specify the first two letters.

To translate a string, wrap it with the "\_" function, such as `_("You have ${} money").format(money)`. Note that the formatter has to be outside of the function. You can also use the "t" string modifier, such as `t"${} money".format(money)`.

If two strings are the same but have to be translated differently, you can add a context string as the first argument, such as `_("the direction", "left")`.

Lastly, if a translated string is stored in a variable, you **have** to use the "\_" function when displaying it, such as `hudHeader(text=_(someVariable))`. Else, "TLErr" will be displayed. Note that you also have to use the "\_" function when storing the string in the variable, else "0" will be displayed.

OverPy will generate and parse .po files for each language based on the name of the main file. You can then use an online editor to edit those files. Leading and trailing whitespace is automatically stripped from the string when put into translation files.

**WARNING**: A translated string cannot be used as a normal string **when stored in a variable**, as it becomes a string array. This means you cannot use `.replace()`, `.charAt()`, etc. When translating your gamemode, look out for these functions.

This also means that, when used in a variable, you cannot use a translated string as an argument of a string: `"{}{}".format(t"string", 1234)` will not work. Instead, do `t"string{}".format(1234)`. The translated string must always be top-level. You will also get "TLErr" if trying to use a translated string as an argument for another function.

You can also potentially save a lot of elements by using the #!translateWithPlayerVar directive (see the associated documentation).

**Note**: The way string formatting works is via the .replace() function and some constants. This means you cannot have the following in your translated strings if using formatters:

- `(0.00, 1.00, 0.00)` (`Vector.UP`)
- `(0.00, -1.00, 0.00)` (`Vector.DOWN`)
- `(1.00, 0.00, 0.00)` (`Vector.LEFT`)
- `(-1.00, 0.00, 0.00)` (`Vector.RIGHT`)
- `(0.00, 0.00, 1.00)` (`Vector.FORWARD`)
- `(0.00, 0.00, -1.00)` (`Vector.BACKWARD`)
- `1876650.25`, `1876651.25`, `1876652.25`, `1876653.25`, `1876654.25`, `1876655.25`, `1876656.25`, `1876657.25`, `1876658.25`, `1876659.25`
If enabled, the compression functions will use a global variable `__compressionAlphabet__` instead of a hardcoded string for the alphabet, which will save further elements.
If specified, the compiled code will also be written to a file with the same name as the main file, but with a `.ws.txt` extension (eg `myGamemode.opy` will produce `myGamemode.ws.txt`).
